scenes.say: Ever wondered why interviewers care so much about mutating arrays? What makes immutability so important in JavaScript?

scenes.label: Immutability
scenes.sub: Methods like map, filter, and reduce return new arrays, keeping your data unchanged.
scenes.say: Map, filter, and reduce always give you a new array. Your original data stays untouched, which makes your code easier to reason about.
Here’s how I double numbers, pick out the evens, and sum them up, all without changing the original array.
Mutating arrays can lead to bugs and confusion. Using immutable methods keeps your data safe and your code predictable.

scenes.question: Is map guaranteed to mutate the array?
scenes.wrong: Yes, map changes the original array.
scenes.right: Nope, map returns a new array and leaves the original untouched.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for this: map never changes the original array. It always returns a new one.
